summary_html: Agency or actor engages in **discriminatory or retaliatory action**, violating civil-rights or placement-equality provisions. Federal statutes prohibit race, religion, sex, or disability bias in placements or investigations.
authority_html:
- **Multiethnic Placement Act (MEPA) & Interethnic Adoption Provisions (IEP)** — prohibits race/ethnicity discrimination in placements  
- **Civil Rights Act (42 U.S.C. § 2000d)** — Title VI discrimination prohibitions in federally funded programs

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the Equal Protection Clause forbids a court from removing a child from a parent's custody because of the racial composition of the parent's household, even where private biases might expose the child to social stigma.
key_cases.relevance: Is the controlling federal authority that race may not drive a custody or placement decision, whatever private prejudices may exist.
key_cases.quote: Classifying persons according to their race is more likely to reflect racial prejudice than legitimate public concerns; the race, not the person, dictates the category.

key_cases.case_name: Humphries v. County of Los Angeles
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that California's Child Abuse Central Index listing scheme deprives listed persons of a protected liberty interest under the stigma-plus test without adequate procedural due process, because California provided no meaningful process to challenge or remove a listing.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the due process framework for challenging a stigmatizing agency listing that restricts employment and licensing.
key_cases.quote: The Humphries have asserted the existence of a sufficient liberty interest under the stigma-plus test, of which they may not be deprived without due process of law.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed the Ninth Circuit in part, holding that Monell's 'policy or custom' requirement applies to section 1983 claims against municipalities for prospective relief as well as for damages, leaving undisturbed the Ninth Circuit's holding that the Child Abuse Central Index listing scheme denied procedural due process.
key_cases.relevance: Requires a person challenging a stigmatizing registry listing to trace the deprivation to a county policy or custom even when only declaratory or injunctive relief is sought.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that Monell's holding applies to §1983 claims against municipalities for prospective relief as well as to claims for damages.
